# Plan: Upgrade Go to 1.26 and Modernize with `go fix`

## Context

The `mcp-todoist` project currently runs on **Go 1.25.7**. Go 1.26 (released February 2026) ships a completely rewritten `go fix` command with 24 modernizer analyzers that automatically transform legacy patterns into idiomatic modern Go. Bumping to 1.26 unlocks the full suite, including the new `errorsastype` and `newexpr` analyzers exclusive to 1.26.

## Codebase Analysis: What `go fix` Will Actually Change

After reading every Go source file, the **primary change** will be the **`any` analyzer** replacing `interface{}` with `any` (~15+ occurrences across the codebase):

| File | Occurrences | Pattern |
|------|------------|---------|
| `internal/todoist/client.go:55` | 1 | `body interface{}` parameter |
| `internal/todoist/projects.go:39,53` | 2 | `map[string]interface{}` params |
| `internal/todoist/tasks.go:52,66` | 2 | `map[string]interface{}` params |
| `internal/todoist/sections.go:30,44` | 2 | `map[string]interface{}` params |
| `internal/todoist/labels.go:25,39` | 2 | `map[string]interface{}` params |
| `internal/todoist/comments.go:33,47` | 2 | `map[string]interface{}` params |
| `internal/tools/tasks.go:122,233` | 2+ | `map[string]interface{}{}` literals |
| `internal/tools/gtd.go:224,260` | 2+ | `map[string]interface{}{}` literals |
| `internal/tools/tools_test.go` | 15+ | `map[string]interface{}{}` in every test |

Other analyzers will likely produce **no changes** because the codebase:
- Has no C-style `for` loops (`rangeint`)
- Has no `HasPrefix`+`TrimPrefix` pairs (`stringscutprefix`)
- Has no `sync.WaitGroup` usage (`waitgroup`)
- Has no `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` in tests (`testingcontext`)
- Has no struct-typed fields with `omitempty` — all are primitives/pointers (`omitzero`)
- Already uses `strings.Builder` correctly (`stringsbuilder`)
- Has no `sort.Slice`, `reflect.TypeOf`, `// +build` constraints, etc.

## Steps

### Step 1: Bump `go.mod` to Go 1.26
- **File:** `go.mod`
- Change `go 1.25.7` → `go 1.26`
- Run `go mod tidy` to update `go.sum`

### Step 2: Preview `go fix` changes
- Run `go fix -diff ./...` to see what the modernizers would change (non-destructive)
- This confirms our analysis before making any changes

### Step 3: Apply `go fix -any` (separate commit)
- Run `go fix -any ./...` to replace all `interface{}` → `any`
- This is the highest-volume change and should be isolated for clean code review
- Per the [Go blog](https://go.dev/blog/gofix), separating `any` into its own commit is recommended

### Step 4: Apply remaining `go fix` analyzers
- Run `go fix ./...` for all remaining default analyzers
- Run `go fix ./...` a second time to catch synergistic fixes

### Step 5: Run tests
- Run `go test -race ./...` to verify no regressions

### Step 6: Update CI/CD workflow
- **File:** `.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml`
- Update `go-version` from `'1.25.7'` to `'1.26'` in both `test` job matrix and `lint` job
- Add `go fix -diff` check step to catch unmodernized code in future PRs

### Commit Strategy
1. `build: bump go directive to 1.26` — go.mod + go.sum
2. `refactor: replace interface{} with any` — go fix -any output
3. `refactor: apply go fix modernizers` — remaining go fix output (if any)
4. `ci: update workflow for Go 1.26 and add go fix check` — CI changes

## Verification
1. `go build ./...` — confirms the code compiles
2. `go test -race ./...` — confirms no behavioral regressions
3. `go vet ./...` — confirms no vet issues
4. `go fix -diff ./...` — confirms no remaining modernization opportunities

name: Build and Test

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]

jobs:
  test:
    name: Build and Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        go-version: ['1.25.7']

    steps:
    - name: Check out code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: ${{ matrix.go-version }}

    - name: Cache Go modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/go/pkg/mod
          ~/.cache/go-build
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ matrix.go-version }}-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ matrix.go-version }}-
          ${{ runner.os }}-go-

    - name: Download dependencies
      run: go mod download

    - name: Verify dependencies
      run: go mod verify

    - name: Build
      run: go build -v ./...

    - name: Run tests
      run: go test -v -race -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./...

    - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
      with:
        files: ./coverage.out
        flags: unittests
        fail_ci_if_error: false

    - name: Run go vet
      run: go vet ./...

    - name: Run staticcheck
      run: |
        go install honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@latest
        staticcheck ./...

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Check out code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: '1.25.7'

    - name: golangci-lint
      uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v8
      with:
        version: v2.6.2
        args: --timeout=5m

## Current Status

golangci-lint supports Go versions that are lower or equal to the Go version used to build it. 

The current binaries from the releases page and the Docker images have been built with go1.25 and will be built with go1.25 as long as go1.26 is not GA, meaning those binaries/images don't support go1.26 (new elements and internal Go changes).

## What's Needed for Go 1.26 Support

In addition to the Go version used to build it, some linters could need to be updated to support newer versions of Go, and internal pieces of golangci-lint could also need to be updated.

## Related Issue

There is an open GitHub issue (#6272) dedicated to tracking Go 1.26 support. Based on the search results, there hasn't been a release yet with Go 1.26 support, though the process follows the same pattern as previous Go version support additions (like Go 1.23, 1.24, and 1.25).

name: Build and Test

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]

jobs:
  test:
    name: Build and Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        go-version: ['1.26']

    steps:
    - name: Check out code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: ${{ matrix.go-version }}

    - name: Cache Go modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/go/pkg/mod
          ~/.cache/go-build
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ matrix.go-version }}-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ matrix.go-version }}-
          ${{ runner.os }}-go-

    - name: Download dependencies
      run: go mod download

    - name: Verify dependencies
      run: go mod verify

    - name: Build
      run: go build -v ./...

    - name: Run tests
      run: go test -v -race -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./...

    - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
      with:
        files: ./coverage.out
        flags: unittests
        fail_ci_if_error: false

    - name: Check go fix modernizers
      run: |
        diff=$(go fix -diff ./... 2>&1)
        if [ -n "$diff" ]; then
          echo "$diff"
          echo "::error::go fix found unmodernized code. Run 'go fix ./...' and commit the changes."
          exit 1
        fi

    - name: Run go vet
      run: go vet ./...

    - name: Run staticcheck
      run: |
        go install honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck@latest
        staticcheck ./...

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Check out code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v5
      with:
        go-version: '1.26'

    - name: golangci-lint
      uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v8
      with:
        version: v2.6.2
        args: --timeout=5m

## Code Review: PR #5 — Upgrade Go to 1.26 and modernize with go fix

### Overview

This PR bumps the Go version from 1.25.7 to 1.26 and applies `go fix -any` to replace all `interface{}` occurrences with the `any` alias. It also updates CI tooling and adds a `go fix -diff` guard to prevent future regressions.

**4 commits, 20 files changed, +64 / -55 lines**

---

### Commit Structure

Clean and well-organized. Each commit is atomic and self-contained:

1. `build: bump go directive to 1.26` — go.mod only
2. `refactor: replace interface{} with any via go fix` — pure mechanical refactor, 18 files
3. `ci: update workflow for Go 1.26 and add go fix check` — CI changes
4. `ci: bump golangci-lint to v2.10.1 for Go 1.26 support` — fix for CI compatibility

---

### Code Changes

**`interface{}` → `any` (18 files)**

All changes are mechanically generated by `go fix -any`. Every substitution is a direct 1:1 replacement with no behavioral change. Correct and complete.

---

### CI Changes

**`go fix -diff` check step** — Good addition. The implementation is sound:

```yaml
diff=$(go fix -diff ./... 2>&1)
if [ -n "$diff" ]; then
  echo "$diff"
  echo "::error::go fix found unmodernized code. Run 'go fix ./...' and commit the changes."
  exit 1
fi
```

One minor observation: redirecting stderr to stdout with `2>&1` captures both the diff output and any potential error messages (e.g., parse failures on malformed Go files). This is fine for a CI gate — a parse error should also fail the step — but worth noting that the error message says "unmodernized code" when it could also be a tooling error. Low concern.

**golangci-lint bump v2.6.2 → v2.10.1** — Necessary and correct. v2.9.0 was the first release with Go 1.26 support.

---

### Potential Issues

- **`go.sum` not in the diff.** The PR description says `go mod tidy` was run, but `go.sum` shows no changes. This is expected since the dependency set didn't change — just confirming it's not a missing file.
- **Commits 3 and 4 could have been squashed** — both touch the same CI file. Commit 4 was a follow-up fix for a CI failure. Not a problem, but squashing before merge would produce a cleaner history.

---

### What Looks Good

- Mechanical changes are isolated from CI changes — easy to review

### Overview

Upgrades Go from 1.25.7 to 1.26, applies `go fix -any` to modernize all `interface{}` to `any`, updates CI tooling, and adds a `go fix -diff` guard. 20 files changed, +66 / -57, 3 commits.

---

1. **`build: bump go directive to 1.26`** — go.mod only

---

- **`interface{}` → `any`** (18 files): All tool-generated, correct 1:1 replacements. No behavioral changes.
- **`fmt.Fprintf` fix** (`gtd.go:122,124`): Replaces `sb.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...))` with `fmt.Fprintf(&sb, ...)` — eliminates intermediate string allocation. Correct fix for staticcheck QF1012.

---

### CI Changes

- **go-version**: `1.25.7` → `1.26` in both jobs
- **golangci-lint**: `v2.6.2` → `v2.10.1` (Go 1.26 support)
- **`go fix -diff` guard**: Catches unmodernized code in future PRs

---

### Verdict

**Approve.** No issues. All changes are mechanical or CI configuration. Tests pass, lint is clean, commit history is tidy. Ready to merge.

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Todoist, written in Go. This server enables Claude and other MCP clients to interact with your Todoist tasks, projects, sections, labels, and comments using natural language. Includes GTD workflow tools for inbox processing and weekly reviews.

This is a Go rewrite of the original [TypeScript implementation](https://github.com/abhiz123/todoist-mcp-server), built with the official [go-sdk v1.3.0](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk).

## Features

- **Full Todoist API Coverage**: 29 tools covering tasks, projects, sections, labels, and comments
- **GTD Workflow Support**: Inbox review, weekly review, task moving, and bulk creation
- **Smart Task Search**: Locate tasks via exact or partial name matching
- **Flexible Filtering**: Organize tasks by due date, priority, project, and more
- **Task ID Support**: Use task IDs directly or search by name

## Available Tools

### Task Tools (6)

| Tool | Description | Key Parameters |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| `todoist_create_task` | Create a new task | `content`, `description`, `due_string`, `priority`, `project_id`, `section_id`, `parent_id`, `labels`, `assignee_id` |
| `todoist_get_tasks` | List tasks with filters | `project_id`, `filter`, `priority`, `limit` |
| `todoist_update_task` | Update a task by ID or name | `task_id`/`task_name`, `content`, `description`, `due_string`, `priority`, `labels`, `assignee_id` |
| `todoist_delete_task` | Delete a task | `task_id`/`task_name` |
| `todoist_complete_task` | Mark a task as complete | `task_id`/`task_name` |
| `todoist_reopen_task` | Reopen a completed task | `task_id`/`task_name` |

### Project Tools (7)

| Tool | Description | Key Parameters |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| `todoist_get_projects` | List all projects | — |

| `todoist_update_project` | Update a project | `project_id`, `name`, `color`, `is_favorite` |
| `todoist_delete_project` | Delete a project | `project_id` |
| `todoist_archive_project` | Archive a project | `project_id` |
| `todoist_unarchive_project` | Unarchive a project | `project_id` |

|------|-------------|----------------|
| `todoist_get_sections` | List sections | `project_id` (optional) |
| `todoist_create_section` | Create a section | `name`, `project_id`, `order` |
| `todoist_update_section` | Update a section | `section_id`, `name` |

## Prerequisites

- Go 1.25.7 or later
- A Todoist account
- Todoist API token

## Getting Your Todoist API Token

1. Log in to [Todoist](https://todoist.com)
2. Go to Settings → Integrations → Developer
3. Copy your API token from the "API token" section

## Installation

### From Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nsega/mcp-todoist.git
cd mcp-todoist
make build
```

The binary will be available at `build/mcp-todoist`.

### Using Go Install

```bash
go install github.com/nsega/mcp-todoist@latest
```

## Usage

### Running Directly

```bash
export TODOIST_API_TOKEN="your_api_token_here"
./build/mcp-todoist
```

### Using Make

```bash
make run TODOIST_API_TOKEN=your_api_token_here
```

## Configuration with Claude Desktop

Add the following to your Claude Desktop configuration file:

**macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
**Windows:** `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
**Linux:** `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "todoist": {
      "command": "/path/to/mcp-todoist",
      "env": {
        "TODOIST_API_TOKEN": "your_api_token_here"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Replace `/path/to/mcp-todoist` with the actual path to your built binary.

## Example Workflows

### GTD Inbox Processing

```
Review my Todoist inbox
→ Runs todoist_inbox_review, shows tasks grouped by age

Move the "research API" task to project Work, section Backlog
→ Runs todoist_move_task with project and section IDs
```

### Weekly Review

```
Run my weekly review
→ Runs todoist_weekly_review, shows project summaries, overdue tasks, undated tasks
```

### Batch Task Creation

```
Create these tasks in my "Reading List" project:
- Read "Thinking, Fast and Slow"
- Read "Deep Work"
- Read "Atomic Habits"
→ Runs todoist_bulk_create_tasks with 3 items
```

### Project Management

```
Show me all my projects
→ Lists all projects with IDs and inbox/favorite status

Create a new project called "Q1 Goals" with board view
→ Creates project with view_style: board
```

## Development

### Building

```bash
make build
```

### Running Tests

```bash
make test
```

### Code Coverage

```bash
make coverage
```

### Linting

```bash
make lint
```

### Running All Checks

```bash
make check
```

### Building for Multiple Platforms

```bash
make build-all
```

- Tasks: CRUD, complete, reopen, search by name or ID
